title: Three US studies supplied within-metric range-size contrasts for individual bird drought responses in a 2024 release
abstract: We tested whether a public bird drought archive permits within-study tests of the link between geographic range size and individual response. The 17 October 2024 release has 80 individual-response rows from 19 studies and 23 species. Only three US studies supply different range sizes within the same response metric. They give 14 study-metric-species units from eight species. With equal study weights and metric intercepts, two studies supply 99.9985% of the within-cell range variation. All three slopes are positive. The pooled slope is +1.071 source effect-size units per tenfold range increase. Study omission slopes range from +0.546 to +1.297. The third study compares range sizes only 1.5% apart. The observed direction agrees with the proposed vulnerability link, but the archive lacks broad within-study support across world regions and independent periods. Shared droughts, small species sets, varied metrics, detection and publication bias limit inference. This is a fixed-release support audit, not a causal effect or a replication with new field data. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure, exact source hashes and external retrieval instructions are included. Pollution and climate-change attribution were not tested.

display.caption: Study coverage and shares of weighted within-cell log-range variation. Only three studies permit within-metric range-size comparisons. Two supply nearly all design variation; shares are not sampling precision.
